subject: Cognitive Science
title: The Straw Man Fallacy
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Straw Man Fallacy.

hook.text: "We should reduce sugar in school lunches." "So you want to starve our children?" That's a straw man.

buildup.text: A straw man distorts an opponent's argument into a weaker version, then attacks the distortion.

discovery.text: It works by substituting an extreme caricature for the real position. The audience may not notice the swap.

twist.text: It's often unintentional. People genuinely misrepresent positions they don't fully understand.

climax.text: The steel man is the antidote: state the opponent's best argument before responding to it.

punchline.text: Fight the real argument, not its shadow.

quiz.question: What is a straw man fallacy?
options: Distorting an argument to make it easier to attack
Attacking the strongest version of an argument
